reviews.one_line_contribution: A head-to-head test of whether a cheap 10-dimensional judge-derived failure-mode signature predicts source-to-target warm-start gain for *textual* reflective prompt optimization better than SPoT-style semantic/task-embedding similarity, with the transfer matrix's split-half reliability measured first as an explicit ceiling on any predictor and an abstaining leave-one-target-out router as the payoff.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Two clusters. (1) SPoT/ATTEMPT and Vu et al. 2020, which the proposal handles correctly: they predict transfer from task embeddings for soft prompts/fine-tuning, and the proposal's claim is a feature-space claim rather than the text-instead-of-soft-prompts domain swap the brief warns about, so these do not sink it. (2) The one that actually threatens it and is never cited: intermediate-task transfer source selection — Pruksachatkun et al. 2020, Poth et al. 2021 ('What to Pre-Train on? Efficient Intermediate Task Selection'), and especially TaskWeb/TaskShop (Kim et al. 2023), which builds a measured source x target transfer matrix over many tasks and uses it to *select* a source, including cheap proxy-score selection. That literature already establishes (a) transfer matrices are worth measuring, (b) semantic/embedding similarity is a mediocre selector, and (c) a cheap proxy score on the target is a strong selector — which is exactly this proposal's predictor (d). Against that backdrop the delta narrows to 'failure signatures are the right feature space, and the setting is reflective text-prompt search', which is real but thinner than the Related Work section implies, and the proposal's own risk factor (4) concedes the contribution collapses if predictor (d) wins.
reviews.strongest_objection: The headline claims are stated at a resolution the design's own unit of generalization cannot resolve. The proposal correctly declares that the bootstrap is clustered on target task 'the unit of generalization' — and there are 8 targets. The power calculation offered (Spearman 0.27 at 80% with 56 cells) is for a single unclustered correlation and does not license Falsifiable Prediction (b), which is a *difference between two dependent correlations* of >=0.2 under target-clustered resampling over 8 clusters; that comparison will not have a CI excluding zero except by luck. Prediction (c) is worse: leave-one-target-out gives 8 router decisions, so the '<=5% vs ~25% negative-transfer incidents' claim rests on roughly 1 versus 6 events out of 24 target-seed cells, whose binomial intervals overlap almost completely, and '>=60% of oracle-minus-cold-start gain' is a ratio of two noisy quantities estimated from 8 held-out targets. This is precisely failure mode 2 the research brief told proposals to avoid. Two secondary objections compound it: (i) the headline Spearman is computed over all 56 cells, so it is inflated or masked by target main effects — the proposal knows this (it includes an additive source+target baseline) but predictions (b) and (d) are stated on raw, not residualized, Delta, and the quantity a router actually needs is the *within-target* ranking of sources, which is 7 items per row; (ii) Delta is pooled across tasks with non-commensurate metrics (MBPP pass rate, GSM8K exact match, HotpotQA F1, instruction-following), so 'test points' are not a common currency and the '6 test points spread' in prediction (a) is not well defined across rows. Third, a conceptual gap in the construct: the failure signature is measured from a *fixed baseline/seed* prompt's failures (step 5), but the artifact being transferred is the *optimized, domain-scrubbed* source prompt, whose residual failure profile is by construction different from the baseline's — the feature describes the task-under-a-bad-prompt while the treatment is a good prompt, and no experiment tests that the signature of the optimized source predicts anything.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Buy statistical resolution instead of breadth of analysis: raise the task count to ~14-16 clusters (cheap, since cells are 50-rollout runs and BBH/SNI supply many clusters) so the router has enough leave-one-target-out folds to support prediction (c), or else demote (c) from a claim to a descriptive figure and make the reliability-plus-predictor comparison the paper. (2) State predictions (b) and (d) on target-residualized Delta and report the within-target rank correlation (mean Spearman across 8 rows of 7) as the primary quantity, since that is what routing consumes; convert Delta to a per-task standardized effect (divide by the step-1 per-task metric SD) before pooling. (3) Pre-register the difference-of-dependent-correlations test with its own power analysis under target-clustered resampling, and report the minimum detectable correlation *gap*, not the minimum detectable correlation. (4) Add the signature of the optimized source prompt (and of the source's residual failures after optimization) as a predictor variant, since that is the object actually being transferred. (5) Resolve the internal inconsistency in Measurement and Noise Control: 'the reflection proposal stream is replayed to remove proposal randomness' is not achievable in the warm-start arm, whose whole treatment is that reflection sees a different starting prompt — say plainly that replay applies only to the null replicate and the re-scoring study. (6) Say explicitly whether the 56-cell matrix is run on both Qwen2.5-7B and 32B or only one; the experiment section reads as both, which roughly doubles the compute and is the only place the budget looks unsafe.
reviews.missing_baseline: A placebo warm start: a well-formed, domain-general instruction skeleton that was never optimized on any source task (role framing + output contract + decomposition + error-avoidance clauses, hand-written or LLM-written to match the scrubbed sources in length and register). Random-source controls for *which* source, but every arm in the plan starts from an optimized artifact, so nothing in the design separates 'transfer of optimization signal' from 'any competent generic prompt beats GEPA's cold seed at 50 rollouts' — and step 8's own finding that gains may be mostly output-format compliance makes that the likely explanation. Secondary omissions a reviewer would also press: (i) a multi-source arm (merge or concatenate the 7 scrubbed sources, or best-of-k warm starts under the same rollout budget), which is the obvious competitor to routing and may beat it outright; (ii) a budget-amortized cold start — warm start at 50 rollouts silently consumes the 300 rollouts spent optimizing the source, so a cold-start arm given a matched *total* budget should be reported alongside the 50-rollout pairing, even if the amortization argument (source cost paid once, reused 7 times) is the one the paper defends.
reviews.preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty. Judged on what the text provides, no preprint search was performed and none is reported anywhere else in the submission: the Related Work names GEPA (2025) and MIPROv2 (2024) but engages only with indexed 2020-2021 soft-prompt transfer work, and its central novelty claim — that no one has measured a reliability-quantified source x target matrix for textual optimized prompts or tested failure-signature versus semantic predictors — is asserted, not searched. That is a weakness, not a neutral, and in this area it is a live risk: warm-starting and prompt-library reuse are the most obvious follow-ups to a 2025 optimizer, GEPA-style systems already ship reusable prompt artifacts, and automatic discovery of domain-general LLM failure taxonomies (rather than the hand-specified 10 modes here) has been an active 2025 preprint topic; any of these could already contain the transfer matrix or the taxonomy-as-feature idea. I cannot name a specific colliding arXiv entry from the submission alone, and establishing that was the authors' burden. Note also that the closest *indexed* threat — TaskWeb/TaskShop and the intermediate-task-selection line — was missed even without a preprint search, which lowers confidence that a search would have been thorough.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A reliability-quantified source-by-target warm-start transfer matrix for *textual* optimized prompts, plus the specific falsifiable claim that a cheap 10-dimensional judge-labeled failure-mode profile predicts that matrix substantially better than SPoT-style semantic/task-embedding similarity, cashed out as a leave-one-target-out router that can abstain to cold start.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Vu et al. 2020 ('Exploring and Predicting Transferability') and SPoT/ATTEMPT are the direct methodological ancestors: they already build a full source-by-target transfer matrix and already test similarity-based predictors of it, including a retrieval rule for picking a source. The proposal concedes the shape is the same and rests its novelty on (a) the medium (text rather than soft prompts) and (b) the predictor (failure signatures rather than task embeddings). The brief itself warns that the medium swap is a modest delta, so essentially all novelty weight lands on (b) — and (b) is itself a composition of two existing pieces: adapter/module routing work (LoraHub, Arrow/MBC-style library routing) already does leave-one-target-out source selection with a fallback, and error-taxonomy-driven prompt optimizers (ProTeGi's beam search over judge-identified error feedback, PromptAgent's error-trace-conditioned MCTS) already treat judge-labeled failure modes as the informative summary of a task. 'Failure modes are the transferable structure' is therefore not a fresh premise; only its use as a *routing feature* is, and that is one idea, not a paper's worth. The genuinely uncontested piece is the split-half reliability measurement of the transfer matrix, which prior transfer studies do not report — but that is a methodological audit, not the advertised claim.
reviews.strongest_objection: Prediction (b) — failure-signature similarity at Spearman 0.45-0.65 versus semantic similarity at 0.0-0.25, a margin of at least 0.2 with a bootstrap CI excluding zero — is not testable with the eight tasks chosen, because across those eight the failure profile is a near-deterministic function of the domain. GSM8K will load on 'arithmetic/bookkeeping slip', MBPP on 'format/contract violation', HotpotQA on 'unsupported claim', the instruction-following set on 'instruction omission'. The two candidate predictors are therefore collinear by construction, and whichever wins is a fact about which sentence encoder was used for the task-embedding arm, not evidence about 'what feature space transfer lives in'. The design needs pairs that dissociate the predictors — semantically near but failure-far, and semantically far but failure-near — and the task-selection criterion never mentions this. Compounding it: only 8 signature vectors exist, so the 56 pairwise similarities have on the order of 8 effective degrees of freedom, the head-to-head is tested by a bootstrap clustered on target (8 clusters), and both correlations are first divided by a split-half reliability estimated from 3 seeds per cell (which cannot even be split into halves evenly). The stated power calculation — Spearman 0.27 detectable at 80% power with 56 cells — is for a *single* correlation with cells treated as independent, which directly contradicts the clustered-bootstrap analysis plan and says nothing about power for the *difference* of two attenuation-corrected correlations. The paper's central number is thus below its own detection threshold, exactly the failure mode the research brief flagged as having sunk the previous round. A secondary technical objection: 'the reflection proposal stream is replayed to remove proposal randomness' is not implementable between warm-start and cold-start arms, since the reflector is conditioned on different prompts and traces in the two arms; fixing a sampling seed does not yield matched proposals, and the pairing is weaker than claimed. Third, there is an unaddressed tension between arm (2)'s domain-scrubbing and prediction (a)'s required 6-point spread between best and worst source: the better the scrub works, the more the sources converge toward a generic skeleton and the more the matrix flattens into noise — the scrubbing step and the signal the paper needs are pulling against each other, and the source-identification leakage test measures the leakage but not this collapse.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: Make predictor dissociation the primary design axis rather than an afterthought: pre-register a task set (16-20 tasks, not 8) containing an explicit discordant subset — at least ~6 pairs that are semantically close but failure-profile distant (e.g., two word-problem sets with different output contracts) and ~6 that are semantically distant but failure-profile close (a code task and an instruction-following task both dominated by contract violations) — and make the correlation restricted to the discordant subset the headline analysis, with the full matrix as secondary. Power the *difference* of correlations at the target-cluster level and report that number, not the single-correlation power at cell level. Report raw uncorrected Spearmans as primary with attenuation correction secondary and a CI on the reliability denominator itself, since a noisy small denominator can manufacture the 0.45-0.65 range. Pre-register what happens to the claim if the signature's discriminative power lives entirely in the format/contract dimension — step (8)(iii) suggests it might, and in that case the finding reduces to 'match the output contract', which should be stated as a pre-committed outcome rather than discovered post hoc. Cut the ablation list (unscrubbed full matrix, Pareto-member variant, second-executor sub-matrix, three taxonomy variants) down to the two that can change a conclusion, and spend the freed compute on more tasks and more seeds per cell.
reviews.missing_baseline: Two, both fatal to the router claim if they win. (1) A task-agnostic generic scaffold seed: one domain-general prompt skeleton (role framing, output contract, decomposition, error-avoidance clauses) authored once by a human or an LLM from *no source task at all*, used as the warm start on every target. 'Best-fixed-source' does not cover this — it is still a source-derived artifact selected on the 7 training targets, so it still presupposes the matrix matters. If a generic scaffold matches the routed source at 50 rollouts, the transfer matrix, the failure taxonomy and the router are all unnecessary, and this is the single most likely outcome given that step (2) deliberately scrubs domain content out of every source prompt. (2) A no-predictor pooling arm: seed the Pareto pool with all 7 scrubbed sources simultaneously and let the optimizer's own validation do the selecting. The ablations mention 'warm start as an extra Pareto-pool member' but only for a single routed source; the all-sources pool is the arm that makes routing moot, and it is cheap because candidate validation is far cheaper than a rollout budget. Minor third: the budget accounting never charges the target run for the failure-signature probe or amortized source optimization, so 'matched budget' is matched only in the arm's favor.
reviews.preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty — no searches reported, no date window, no arXiv sweep, no named near-misses. Related Work cites SPoT (2021), Vu et al. (2020), ATTEMPT, APE, OPRO, PromptBreeder, MIPROv2 (2024) and GEPA (2025); everything but GEPA is an indexed paper more than a year old, which is precisely the citation profile the reviewing standard here treats as inadequate. This is a weakness, not a neutral: in a subarea where GEPA follow-ups, prompt-library/module-routing methods, and domain-general LLM failure taxonomies (e.g., the 2025 multi-agent failure-taxonomy line of work, which constructs exactly the kind of pre-registered domain-general failure catalogue this proposal's step (5) needs) have all appeared within months, the probability that the specific pairing 'judge-labeled failure taxonomy as a source-selection feature' is untouched cannot be assessed from what the authors provide. I did not search and so cannot name a definitive scoop, but the burden of establishing novelty sits with the submission and has not been discharged; I am discounting novelty by roughly two points on this basis alone, and a discovered collision on the failure-taxonomy-as-routing-feature idea would move this to a clear reject, since the reliability audit alone would then be the whole contribution.

reviews.one_line_contribution: A reliability-quantified source x target warm-start transfer matrix for textual (not soft) optimized prompts under a matched 50-rollout budget, plus a head-to-head test that a cheap 10-dimensional judge-labeled failure-mode signature predicts realized transfer gain better than SPoT-style semantic/task-embedding similarity, closed by a leave-one-target-out router that can abstain to cold start.
reviews.closest_prior_work: Su et al., 'On Transferability of Prompt Tuning for Natural Language Processing' (NAACL 2022) is the work that most threatens novelty, and the proposal does not cite it. It already (i) measures a full cross-task prompt transfer matrix, (ii) uses transferred prompts as initialization to accelerate subsequent optimization -- exactly the warm-start setting here -- and (iii) reports that a *non-semantic* similarity measure (overlap of activated neurons) predicts transferability substantially better than task-embedding/semantic similarity. The structural claim under review -- 'transfer lives in a feature space other than subject matter, and SPoT-style semantic similarity is a weak predictor' -- is therefore already on the record; what remains new is the particular feature space (a hand-specified, judge-labeled failure taxonomy), the text-prompt/reflective-optimizer setting, and the abstaining router. By the research brief's own standard that 'they used soft prompts, we use text' is a domain swap rather than a contribution, the delta over Su et al. is one new similarity feature plus a router, which is a modest rather than a strong novelty claim. On the warm-start-transfer-of-text side, meta-learned system-prompt initialization work from 2025 (e.g. 'System Prompt Optimization with Meta-Learning'/MetaSPO) already transfers textual prompts to unseen tasks as initialization, though it does not predict per-pair gain or abstain. SPoT/ATTEMPT and Vu et al. 2020, the works the proposal does name, are the weaker threats precisely because they are the semantic-predictor position being argued against.
reviews.strongest_objection: The design's own generalization unit is 8 task clusters, and the two headline predictions are stated at a resolution that 8 clusters cannot resolve -- the exact failure mode ('effects below the design's own detection threshold') the brief warned against. Prediction (b) asks for failure-signature similarity to exceed semantic similarity by >= 0.2 Spearman with a bootstrap CI excluding zero, and the Measurement section justifies this with a power calculation over 56 cells ('detects a Spearman of ~0.27 at 80% power') -- but the pre-registered analysis is a bootstrap clustered on target task, i.e. resampling 8 units, and a mixed model with source and target random effects. The 56 cells are 8x7 crossings of the same 8 tasks; they are not 56 independent observations, so the stated MDE is computed under an independence assumption the authors themselves reject two sentences later. With 8 clusters, cluster-bootstrap CIs on a *difference of correlations* are wide and badly calibrated, and a 0.2 gap is very unlikely to clear them. Prediction (c) is worse: 'router recovers >= 60% of the oracle-minus-cold-start gain' is estimated from exactly 8 leave-one-target-out folds, one realized accuracy per held-out target, against a per-run test SD of ~3 points that the authors measure themselves; the interval on that ratio will span most of [0,1], and the companion claim of <= 5% vs ~25% negative-transfer incidents is a comparison of proportions over 8 routing decisions. A second, independent objection: the failure taxonomy is dominated by contract-shaped modes (format/contract violation, instruction omission, over-generation, premature termination), so tasks that share an output contract will share a failure signature *and* benefit from a warm start that supplies that contract. The likely finding is then 'shared output format predicts transfer' -- the boring explanation the brief names -- and prediction (d) does not guard against it, because it controls only for checkpoint-0 score, not for answer-format match. Third: the head-to-head is asymmetric. The failure-signature arm gets a family of variants (cosine vs 1-JS, 10 vs 50 traces, coarsened to 3 modes, signatures over successes as well as failures) while the semantic arm gets essentially one; over a 56-cell matrix with 8 clusters that is a garden of forking paths that can manufacture the predicted 0.2 gap.
reviews.what_would_fix_it: (1) Buy degrees of freedom at the generalization unit: go to ~16-20 source tasks and pay for it by dropping the second-executor 4x3 sub-matrix, the unscrubbed-source matrix, and the seed-vs-Pareto-member arm, which are ablations no reviewer is demanding before the main claim is established. (2) Pre-register one failure-signature variant (one similarity function, one trace count, one taxonomy granularity) as the confirmatory predictor and demote the rest to clearly labelled exploratory analyses. (3) Add an output-contract/answer-type match indicator as both a competing predictor in step 6 and a control in prediction (d) alongside checkpoint-0 score; the failure-signature claim survives only if its partial correlation stays >= 0.3 after controlling for *both*. (4) Restate the router claim as a per-target paired difference against best-fixed-source with a target-clustered interval, not a percentage-of-oracle point estimate, and recompute all MDEs under the clustered analysis actually planned rather than under n=56 independence. (5) Actually run and report the preprint search. (6) Drop or justify 'the reflection proposal stream is replayed to remove proposal randomness' -- reflections are conditioned on the current candidate prompt, which differs by construction between the warm and cold arms, so the replay is not well defined and the hedge 'where feasible' hides that.
reviews.missing_baseline: Multi-source warm start: seeding the target run with all 7 scrubbed source prompts at once (as the initial Pareto pool) or with a single merged/meta-optimized prompt distilled from the 7 training sources, in the MetaSPO style. This is the obvious deployable alternative that makes source selection unnecessary, it costs no more rollouts than single-source warm start under GEPA's pool mechanics, and if it matches the oracle-source cell the entire router contribution evaporates -- yet it appears nowhere in the router baseline list, which stops at best-fixed-source. A close second omission is a source-free placebo: a hand-written or LLM-written generic instruction skeleton of matched length and structure, derived from no task. Without it, 'random source' cannot separate 'transfer of task-specific structure' from 'any longer, better-engineered starting prompt helps', and the additive source-main-effect model tests only whether sources differ, not whether their content matters at all.
reviews.preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and nothing elsewhere in the submission substitutes for it: the Related Work section is organized around indexed work (SPoT 2021, Vu et al. 2020, ATTEMPT, APE, OPRO, PromptBreeder) plus two named systems (MIPROv2 2024, GEPA 2025), and reports no searches, no date range, and no negative findings. Per the review instruction, that is a weakness rather than a neutral, and it bites hard here because 'warm-start GEPA on task B from the prompt it found on task A' is an obvious enough idea that the 2025-2026 preprint stream is the single most likely place it has already been tried. Concrete collision candidates the authors must clear and did not mention: meta-learned/transferable system-prompt optimization (e.g. 'System Prompt Optimization with Meta-Learning', 2025), which already warm-starts textual prompts on unseen tasks; the 2025 wave of cross-task and library-based prompt-optimization systems (PromptWizard, Trace/TextGrad-style optimizers, AutoPDL) that reuse optimized instructions across tasks; and error-taxonomy-driven prompt repair, which supplies half the proposed feature space. Separately, the pre-2025 literature the check should have surfaced includes Su et al. 2022 on prompt-tuning transferability, which already reports the non-semantic-predictor-beats-semantic-predictor result in soft-prompt space; missing a 2022 NAACL paper that anticipates the structural claim suggests the novelty search was thin in both directions, not just the recent one.
